The three given vertices are (5,3), (6,8), and (7,4). In a parallelogram, the diagonals bisect each other, so the sum of the coordinates of one pair of opposite vertices equals the sum of the coordinates of the other pair. We test the three possible pairings of the known vertices to find the fourth vertex \((x,y)\) with \(x > 7\):

- If (5,3) and (6,8) are opposite: \((5+6, 3+8) = (7+x, 4+y) \Rightarrow (11,11) = (7+x,4+y) \Rightarrow x=4, y=7\) (not \(x>7\)).
- If (5,3) and (7,4) are opposite: \((5+7, 3+4) = (6+x, 8+y) \Rightarrow (12,7) = (6+x,8+y) \Rightarrow x=6, y=-1\) (not \(x>7\)).
- If (6,8) and (7,4) are opposite: \((6+7, 8+4) = (5+x, 3+y) \Rightarrow (13,12) = (5+x,3+y) \Rightarrow x=8, y=9\) (satisfies \(x>7\)).

Thus the fourth vertex is \((8,9)\), and \(x + y = 8 + 9 = 17\).

Answer: 17
